result:
Good — the full suite compiles and the only failures across all `*AgentTest.java` files are my 3, confirming they're isolated to `Entities`.

**Summary:** Wrote `src/test/org/apache/commons/lang/EntitiesAgentTest.java` with 35 self-contained JUnit 3.8 tests (matching this project's style) covering the XML/HTML32/HTML40 entity sets, escape/unescape round-tripping (named entities, decimal/hex numeric references, malformed input, the `&...&...;` edge case), the Writer-based overloads, and each of the package-private `EntityMap` implementations (`ArrayEntityMap`, `BinaryEntityMap`, `HashEntityMap`, `TreeEntityMap`, `LookupEntityMap`).

3 tests fail, each exposing a genuine bug in `Entities.java`:

1. **`testEntityNameNegativeValueDoesNotThrow`** and **`testLookupEntityMapNegativeValueDoesNotThrow`** — `LookupEntityMap.name(int)` (line 511) does `if (value < LOOKUP_TABLE_SIZE) return lookupTable()[value];` without checking for negative values, so any negative input throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning `null` like every other `EntityMap` implementation does for an unknown value.

2. **`testBinaryEntityMapDuplicateValueAtFirstSlotIsIgnored`** — `BinaryEntityMap.add(String, int)` (line 669) checks `if (insertAt > 0) return;` to detect "value already present" (binary search returns a non-negative index on a hit), but a hit at index `0` fails that check, falls through into the insert logic, and corrupts `insertAt` into `-1`, causing `System.arraycopy` to throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of silently ignoring the duplicate (as the class's own code comment says it should).
